When BitChord finds a better copy of the playing song, such as your Telegram FLAC after it started from YouTube, it’s loaded in the background and faded in at the same point. If that can’t happen, the switch happens the usual way.

When your Telegram file has a song’s title but a different length, it’s usually another recording, so BitChord plays the song from elsewhere. With this on, the patch listens to the first 15 seconds of the song as it plays and compares them with the start of the Telegram file. If they’re the same recording, the file is used the next time the song plays.

Each check downloads up to the first 45 seconds of the Telegram file, about 5 to 15 MB for a lossless file, and uses some battery for a few seconds. Nothing is uploaded or sent anywhere else.
While this is on, BitChord’s equaliser is turned off and Battery saver stands down, so the sound isn’t equalised twice and songs stay off the audio chip, where JamesDSP couldn’t hear them.

With suggestions on, when a song plays from another source the patch searches your selected chats for that artist and suggests a file whose title is a few letters off. Nothing is renamed until you accept. Saving a name also removes BitChord’s saved copy of that song, so its next play uses your Telegram file.

You don’t own a private channel yet. Create one in Telegram, without a public link, and come back.
Your account is ready to stream music.
Your community channels are checked for new posts every few hours while BitChord is open, and new files are copied too. They count toward the same hourly limit.
Your main channel then lists the music in the opposite order to the community channel. Applies to channels copying hasn’t started from yet.

Your phone talks to Telegram directly. Your API details are encrypted on this phone and your Telegram session is stored privately. The session is a normal Telegram login, so it can reach your whole account, not just music. Audio BitChord has saved stays until you clear it, even after you sign out. You can end the session anytime in the official Telegram app under Settings → Devices.
Your searches also check the selected chats for a match. To tell 16-bit from 24-bit, or Dolby Atmos from other Dolby files, the start of a few files per search is downloaded.
